advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Provide an operator-facing entry point (CLI subcommand) for `BindingStore.unretire`, or reword the alert remedy to point at an actually-available operator action.
evidence: binding_store.py:695: `"remedy": f"BindingStore.unretire({jira_key!r}) to re-enable creation"`
A repo-wide search for `unretire` finds only the method definition, docs/ADR text, and tests — no CLI/command wiring that exposes it to operators.
advisory.finding: The suppression alert and ADR present `BindingStore.unretire(<jira_key>)` as the operator remedy, but `unretire` is a Python method with no operator-facing CLI/command surface, so an operator reading the bridge alert cannot invoke the documented route back without writing code.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that constructs a FRESH BindingStore over an already-written bindings-retired.json (separate instance from the one that retired) and asserts retired_key_for_local/is_retired_local resolve and the create is suppressed.
evidence: _retired_store retires within one live instance: `store.bind_confirm(...)` then `for _ in range(...): store.note_absent(jira_key)` — never reloads (test_no_resurrection_after_confirmed_delete_3b5f.py:79-86)
_retire updates the map in memory: `self._retired_locals[local_id] = jira_key` (binding_store.py:586), so tests get a populated map regardless of the __init__ path

The real production path is the __init__ comprehension over the FILE: `self._retired_locals = {str(entry['local_id']): key for key, entry in self._retired_entries().items() ...}` (binding_store.py:175-179) — each reconcile pass loads a fresh BindingStore, so cross-pass suppression depends on THIS reconstruction, which no test exercises

retired_key_for_local returns None unless the key is both in _retired_locals AND _retired (binding_store.py:640-641) — a wrong local_id key in the __init__ comprehension would silently return None (fail to suppress) with all current tests still green
advisory.finding: The production tombstone path — BindingStore reconstructing _retired_locals from bindings-retired.json at __init__ — is untested; every test populates _retired_locals via the same-instance in-memory _retire update, which masks the __init__ reconstruction.
advisory.suggested_fix: After _retired_store retires the pairing, drop the instance and build a new `BindingStore(repo_root / '.tickets-tracker')` over the same tracker dir, then assert `store2.retired_key_for_local('loc-1') == 'DIG-1'` and that compute_outbound_mutations on store2 suppresses the create.
